newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool indicator rises 7 cents to 726c/kg.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool indicator rises 7 cents to 726c/kg.

text.p: The Australian wool market eastern indicator rose seven cents to 726 cents a kg clean on Thursday at sales in Sydney and Melbourne, Wool International said.
This was the highest level since late August 1995.
Merino fleece was dearer, with 19/21 microns slightly dearer, 20m 0.5 percent dearer, 22/24m 1.5 percent dearer, and 23/25/26m two percent dearer.
Merino skirtings were up to two percent dearer.
In crossbreds, 27/28/29m were up to two percent dearer, with 30/31m 1.5 percent dearer, with crossbred skirtings one percent dearer.
In cardings, lambs were unchanged, locks one percent dearer, and crutchings slightly dearer.
WI said Japanese interests including China were principal buyers with good support from Western Europe.
Of the 24,068 bales offered, 4.7 percent were passed in.
Sales continue next week in Sydney, Adelaide and Fremantle with about 77,000 bales to be offered.
